questionText: How do you change the server port in Spring Boot?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can set server.port through the appropriate source, use a random test port, and distinguish the application listener from surrounding network routing.
inScope: File, environment, system, and command-line forms

claims.statement: Spring Boot's embedded web server reads server.port, whose documented default for the normal server is 8080, and the property can be externally overridden.
Setting server.port to zero asks the operating system to allocate an available port, and a Spring Boot web integration test can inject the selected port with @LocalServerPort.
Changing the process listening port does not automatically change a container port publication, reverse-proxy route, firewall rule, service registry, or health-check target.

examples.title: Compile and run the exact random-port integration test

validation.command: Run mvn -o -q test with Java 17 and Spring Boot 3.3.1 against the exact HttpSmokeTest plus a minimal @SpringBootConfiguration fixture
validation.expected: Tomcat starts on an operating-system assigned port and @LocalServerPort injects a value greater than zero

visuals.title: Five ways to supply or select the server port

notes: The test initially failed in the filesystem sandbox because socket binding was denied, then passed unchanged in the approved local execution context.

review.notes: The default port, external forms, random-port behavior, and @LocalServerPort package were checked against Spring Boot 3.3.1 documentation and metadata; the exact integration test passed on Java 17.
